 DES MOINES, Iowa — Iowa Senior Medicare Patrol is warning that scammers are using AI and advanced technology to target older adults with Medicare fraud during the open enrollment period, which runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7.
 The U.S. General Accounting Office estimates that $60 billion is lost nationally each year to Medicare fraud. Scammers are actively targeting Medicare beneficiaries with fake plan offers, phishing texts and impostor calls.
 "Medicare fraud is not just a financial crime against the government – it directly harms Iowans," Griffith said. "When a scammer steals your Medicare number, they can submit fraudulent Medicare claims, leaving you unable to get legitimate care when you need it most."
 SHIIP-SMP Director Kristin Griffith said Medicare fraud can be difficult to spot, especially when scammers can fake familiar phone numbers and create believable medical bills. The organization is encouraging Iowans to watch out for common scams.
 One scam involves callers claiming to be from Medicare offering a new plastic or chip-enabled Medicare card. Medicare cards do not expire and are not being replaced with plastic or chip-enabled cards, and Medicare does not provide cards with special benefits.
 Another scam involves threats of coverage cancellation unless personal information or Medicare numbers are provided. Medicare representatives will never cold-call, text or email demanding personal details.
 Scammers also use advertisements or solicitors promising cash cards, free medical equipment or dramatic coverage upgrades in exchange for a Medicare number. To review options or change Medicare coverage, people should go directly to Medicare.gov or call 1-800-MEDICARE.
 Iowa Senior Medicare Patrol recommends several steps to protect against fraud. People should treat their Medicare card like a credit card and never share the number with anyone who contacts them unsolicited by phone, text, email or at their doorstep.
 If someone receives a questionable message from Medicare, they should hang up and go directly to Medicare.gov or call 1-800-MEDICARE. People should not click links in text messages or emails and should type web addresses directly into their browser to avoid fraud sites.
 Anyone who suspects their Medicare number has been compromised or notices unfamiliar charges on a Medicare Summary Notice or Explanation of Benefits should call the Iowa SMP at 1-800-351-4664 or report online at iowa.gov/prevent-fraud/report-fraud .
